sub_graphs.title: Capella: Light Client Trust Boundaries
sub_graphs.description: Models the trust boundaries in the Capella light client protocol, focusing on what external data is trusted and how

nodes.label: Untrusted Update Received
nodes.description: A LightClientUpdate or LightClientFinalityUpdate has been received from an untrusted source

nodes.label: Verify Sync Committee Signatures
nodes.description: Verify that the update is signed by a sufficient number of the current sync committee members

nodes.label: Verify Finality Merkle Proof
nodes.description: Verify the Merkle branch proving the finalized header against the attested header's state root

nodes.label: Verify Execution Payload Proof
nodes.description: Verify the Merkle branch proving execution payload header against beacon body root (Capella addition)

nodes.label: Update Cryptographically Verified
nodes.description: The update has passed all cryptographic verifications and can be applied to advance the light client state

edges.label: Finality proof valid; verify execution proof

external_entities.name: Untrusted Light Client Server
external_entities.description: Any node providing light client data, which may be malicious or compromised

ambiguities.text: The specification does not define the minimum number of sync committee signatures required to accept an update.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume the threshold is inherited from the Altair light client spec (typically > 1/3 of the 512-member sync committee). This is a critical security parameter that should be verified.

ambiguities.text: EXECUTION_PAYLOAD_GINDEX = 25 is defined without explaining its derivation from the BeaconBlockBody Merkle tree structure.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume gindex 25 corresponds to the correct position of the execution_payload field in the generalized Merkle tree of BeaconBlockBody. This is a constant that must match the SSZ container field ordering.

implicit_assumptions.description: The light client trusts that the sync committee was honestly elected and that a supermajority of committee members are honest.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: A corrupted sync committee could sign fraudulent headers, causing the light client to accept an invalid chain state including incorrect execution payload data.

implicit_assumptions.description: The light client can connect to at least one honest full node to receive correct bootstrap and update data.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: If all connected servers are malicious, the light client could be bootstrapped onto a fake chain, even with valid-looking signatures from a dishonest sync committee majority.
